---
title: "Walkthrough"
description: "Take the Sandcastle-produced branch and turn its greeting into a Crossplane XR ready for the Hello Pico on Kubernetes composition."
---

## Overview of what you will do

1. Confirm the Sandcastle lab has produced its durable branch.
2. Run `handoff.sh` to read the greeting `value` and emit a
   Crossplane XR (`work/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/build/xr.yaml`).
3. Diff the generated XR against the reference `05-xr.yaml` from the
   Kubernetes lab.
4. (Optional) Apply the generated XR on a running Crossplane cluster
   configured from the
   [Hello Pico on Kubernetes lab](../hello-pico-on-kubernetes/index.qmd).

Run every command from the root of your local clone of the academy
repository.

## Step 1 · Confirm the Sandcastle branch exists

```bash
git -C work/hello-world-pico-sandcastle/target-repo \
    rev-parse sandcastle/hello-world-pico

git -C work/hello-world-pico-sandcastle/target-repo \
    show sandcastle/hello-world-pico:rules/hello.yaml
```

You should see one commit hash and a three-line YAML with
`value: "Hello, Pico!"`. If the branch does not exist, run the
[Hello World Pico Sandcastle lab](../hello-world-pico-sandcastle/walkthrough.qmd)
first, or let this lab's `verify.sh` do it for you.

## Step 2 · Run the hand-off

```bash
bash labs/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/downloads/handoff.sh
```

The script reads the `value:` field from the rule on the branch and
writes an `XHelloWorldPico` XR:

```bash
cat work/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/build/xr.yaml
```

Expected output (the leading comment lines are informational):

```yaml
apiVersion: oe.academy/v1alpha1
kind: XHelloWorldPico
metadata:
  name: hello
spec:
  value: "Hello, Pico!"
```

## Step 3 · Diff against the reference XR

The reference XR the Kubernetes lab already ships lives at
`labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/downloads/05-xr.yaml`. The generated XR
must match its `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.name`, and `spec.value`:

```bash
diff -u \
  <(grep -E '^(apiVersion|kind|  name|  value):' \
        labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/downloads/05-xr.yaml) \
  <(grep -E '^(apiVersion|kind|  name|  value):' \
        work/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/build/xr.yaml)
```

An empty diff (exit code 0) is the pass. The lab's automatable
[`verify.sh`](downloads/verify.sh) performs the equivalent check
programmatically.

## Step 4 · (Optional) Apply on a real cluster

If you already have a Crossplane cluster set up per the
[Hello Pico on Kubernetes walkthrough](../hello-pico-on-kubernetes/walkthrough.qmd)
steps 1–4, you can apply the generated XR without modification:

```bash
kubectl apply -f work/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/build/xr.yaml

bash labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/downloads/verify.sh
```

Cluster-side verification is intentionally delegated to the
Kubernetes lab so this lab stays scoped to the hand-off boundary.

## Step 5 · Cleanup

```bash
rm -rf work/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes
```

The Sandcastle lab's `work/` root is intentionally left untouched — it
is still the durable input to this hand-off.

## Automatable verification

The lab ships an end-to-end
[`verify.sh`](downloads/verify.sh) that runs the Sandcastle lab (if
needed), runs the hand-off, and asserts the generated XR matches the
Kubernetes lab's `05-xr.yaml`:

```bash
bash labs/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/downloads/verify.sh
```

Expected final line:

```
verify: OK — xr=<path>/xr.yaml value="Hello, Pico!" (matches labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/downloads/05-xr.yaml)
```
